I worry about covered call strategies if we have a 2009 recession or another incident like COVID.  I need data for those once in a generation situations.

JEPQ gives you monthly cash flow now, SCHD builds growing income over time, and ETLGX adds diversification. That's not a bad starting trio at all.

Dividends dont matter its the shareprice that generates wealth. However the dividend give you a discount on the shareprice once they pay it.
Example company worth 100 dollars per share pay you 5 dollars dividend now the price drops 95 dollars. You can DRIP it and buy for 95 dollars instead of 100 dollars.
There was a reason the company that went to 100 dollars so the potential of this company to return to this shareprice is very high. Thus giving 5 dollars upsite each time they pay(rebuying).
This is why Chevron is better then Nvidia here. Your goal as investor is to gain more shares which means ownership of the company. This is how snowball works, you get more ownership for more dividend
That’s a good way of putting it. Comparing those two companies as dividend plays is night and day.
